limitation: A narrative clinical review synthesizes evidence but does not itself test an intervention.

title: Large evidence review evaluates synthetic and biologic DMARDs
summary: A systematic literature review assessed the efficacy of conventional, biologic, and targeted synthetic DMARDs, plus glucocorticoids, to inform EULAR's latest recommendations.
whyItMatters: It exposes the evidence base behind the guideline rather than only the final recommendations.
limitation: A broad review can establish comparative patterns but cannot predict an individual's response or side effects.

title: EULAR updates its rheumatoid arthritis treatment recommendations
summary: The 2025 update covers methotrexate, short-term glucocorticoids, biologic DMARDs including etanercept, biosimilars, and JAK inhibitors using newly reviewed efficacy and safety evidence.
whyItMatters: This is one of the highest-level current summaries of how specialists sequence RA medicines and adjust treatment when targets are not met.
limitation: Guidelines describe population-level care and do not determine which treatment is right for one person.
source: Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases / PubMed

title: Current Enbrel label emphasizes serious-infection and TB precautions
summary: The current U.S. label directs clinicians to test for latent TB, begin TB treatment before Enbrel when positive, and monitor for active TB and other serious infections during therapy.
whyItMatters: This is the primary U.S. safety source for etanercept, not a rewritten drug-information page.
limitation: The label does not set one universal interval between starting latent-TB therapy and starting Enbrel.
source: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine

title: Hawaii's official medical cannabis registry and access information
summary: The state portal explains Hawaii's medical cannabis registry, qualifying-patient process, current rules, and official program contacts.
whyItMatters: Legal access details should come from Hawaii rather than dispensary marketing or generic national summaries.
limitation: Program rules can change; this link is legal and administrative information, not evidence that cannabis treats RA inflammation.
source: State of Hawaii Department of Health

title: CDC guidance explains short-course latent-TB treatment
summary: CDC preferentially recommends short-course rifamycin-based regimens for many people and warns that rifampin and related medicines can substantially alter the effects of other drugs.
whyItMatters: It explains why latent TB is treated before TNF-inhibitor therapy and why a full medication-interaction review matters.
limitation: The appropriate regimen and timing depend on clinical circumstances, interactions, and exclusion of active TB.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: A practical starting point for living with rheumatoid arthritis
summary: The American College of Rheumatology collects patient fact sheets on RA, methotrexate, exercise, self-management, and treatment choices in one maintained resource.
whyItMatters: It is a reliable map for a newly diagnosed person who needs durable basics before interpreting daily research news.
limitation: Patient guidance is intentionally broad and is not a substitute for an individualized treatment plan.

title: What the ACR says to know about methotrexate
summary: This maintained patient guide explains expected timing, common monitoring, infection precautions, pregnancy warnings, and when to contact a rheumatology provider.
whyItMatters: Methotrexate is often the anchor RA drug; knowing what is routine and what deserves a call can make the first months less opaque.
limitation: The fact sheet cannot account for your dose, laboratory results, other medicines, or medical history.

title: Prednisone: benefits, tradeoffs, and monitoring basics
summary: The ACR patient guide describes why prednisone is used for inflammatory disease and reviews common short- and long-term concerns.
whyItMatters: Steroids can relieve symptoms quickly while slower RA medicines take effect, but dose and duration materially affect risk.
limitation: Never change or abruptly stop a prescribed steroid based on general web content.

title: Cannabis and chronic pain: what the evidence can and cannot establish
summary: NCCIH summarizes research on cannabis and cannabinoids for chronic pain, along with adverse effects, product variability, and gaps in long-term evidence.
whyItMatters: It offers a federal evidence review without assuming that pain findings from mixed conditions automatically apply to inflammatory RA.
limitation: RA-specific evidence is limited, products and doses vary widely, and symptom relief is not the same as controlling inflammation or joint damage.
source: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health

title: ACR weighs exercise, diet, rehabilitation, and other integrative RA approaches
summary: The ACR's integrative treatment guideline evaluates exercise, rehabilitation, diet, and selected complementary approaches alongside disease-modifying treatment.
whyItMatters: It separates supported self-management options from claims that are popular but weakly tested.
limitation: Integrative measures complement rather than replace DMARD treatment that prevents joint damage.

title: Vaccination guidance for people taking rheumatic-disease medicines
summary: ACR guidance discusses vaccine timing and how immune-modifying medicines can affect response, including specific considerations around methotrexate.
whyItMatters: Vaccination planning is especially relevant before and during biologic therapy.
limitation: Medication holds and vaccine timing should be decided with the prescribing clinician; live vaccines require particular care.

title: What FDA oversight does—and does not—mean for supplements
summary: FDA explains that dietary supplements are regulated differently from drugs and generally are not approved for safety and effectiveness before sale.
whyItMatters: A product being sold legally does not establish that it works for RA or that it is compatible with methotrexate, prednisone, rifampin, or Enbrel.
limitation: This is regulatory context, not an assessment of any one supplement.

title: Complementary approaches for RA: evidence, gaps, and interaction cautions
summary: NCCIH reviews complementary approaches studied for RA and emphasizes the limited evidence for many products, possible interactions, and the importance of not replacing conventional care.
whyItMatters: It provides a useful first-pass screen before spending money or combining supplements with prescription medicines.
limitation: Evidence changes and supplement quality varies; a category-level review cannot validate a specific brand or dose.
source: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health

title: Homeopathy: a candid review of the evidence and safety issues
summary: NCCIH reports that there is little evidence supporting homeopathy for any specific health condition and notes that some products labeled homeopathic can contain active ingredients.
whyItMatters: It distinguishes homeopathy from herbal products and explains why 'natural' or highly diluted does not automatically mean useful or risk-free.
limitation: This is a broad evidence review rather than an RA-specific clinical trial.
source: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health
